claims.text: The local row, Bulbapedia, and PokeBoon place the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 4 Sunkern insert on August 23, 2000; Bulbapedia's volume list gives ISBN 4889917578 for volume 4.
Bulbapedia identifies volume 4 as the fourth of six How I Became a Pokemon Card manga volumes created by Kagemaru Himeno and states that its included promo card is Sunkern.
Bulbapedia lists the first edition as a Japanese Kadokawa-Media Factory publication dated August 23, 2000 with ISBN 4889917578.
The local source slice models one source-pinned card row for this route: Sunkern source index 206.
Bulbapedia describes How I Became a Pokemon Card as a manga where each standalone story expands on the image shown on an actual Pokemon card, explaining what the Pokemon is doing or how it got there.
PokeBoon credits the Sunkern promo illustration to Kagemaru Himeno / 姫野かげまる; Bulbapedia identifies Himeno as the creator of How I Became a Pokemon Card.

Bulbapedia's Himeno page identifies her as a TCG illustrator and creator of How I Became a Pokemon Card, plus related Pokemon manga/book work including Pokemon Tales, Pokemon Card GB The Comix, and Himemaru: Pokemon Card Explorer.

Bulbapedia's Sunkern card page says the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional print is commonly known as Natta Wake Sunkern and that its border text reads Pokemon Card Books How I Became a Pokemon Card bonus card.
PokeBoon identifies Sunkern and Spearow as Pokemon depicted in the Sunkern promo card illustration.

Agents should keep this Vol. 4 Sunkern route separate from Neo Genesis Sunkern, Neo Destiny Sunkern, modern Sunkern cards, generic Natta Wake lots, Sunkern-line Sunflora listings, and the other How I Became a Pokemon Card volume inserts.

The catalog can make the Vol. 4 book route, Natta Wake nickname, Sunkern/Spearow illustration context, and Sunkern row identity legible, but it does not prove seller possession, authenticity, condition, price, complete book/insert state, or spendability.

narrative.human_title: How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 4 — the small seed gets a whole story
narrative.why_it_matters: Sunkern is exactly why this manga route matters. A price-first collector might skip past it as a tiny Grass Pokemon, but Himeno's project asks the better question: what would make this picture worth becoming a card? Volume 4 turns that quiet seed into a story-object. The route, the book, the border text, the Spearow in the scene, and Himeno's authorship all say the same thing: Pokemon was assembled not only from mascots and chase cards, but from little scenes someone cared enough to explain.

card_highlights.why_it_matters: Sunkern matters here because it is not trying to overpower the binder. It is the perfect Natta Wake subject: a small seed Pokemon whose meaning comes from scene, story, and route. The card asks for patience, which is exactly what a good collector-agent should have.

narrative.human_title: Sunkern — Natta Wake Vol. 4, the patient little scene
narrative.why_it_matters: This Sunkern is wonderfully quiet. It is not here to dominate a showcase; it is here because Himeno's whole project says small Pokemon deserve scenes, motives, and stories too. The card becomes collectible because the book teaches you how to look at it. That is a different kind of chase: not the chase for the biggest name, but the chase for the little assembly that would otherwise disappear.
